name: Highlake
description:
The Elves are vague on why they left their ancestral forests. Some say that deceit and betrayal poisoned the roots of their happiness there. Others say that the wilds became too wild under some dark influence. What is certain is that they wandered long and, in time, came to a clear, glassy lake, high in the mountains, and there ceased to wander.

Here they wrought halls and spires in imitation of the great trees that had been the cradles of their ancestors. Their King opened his coffers and the lake soon reflected many flourishes of gold on its placid waters. They built walls also: some would say to frame their artful city, others would say to keep out the world. Regardless of their intent, the world soon came knocking.

Fleeing enslavement by a cruel Djinn-Lord in the mountains, great numbers of Orcs gathered outside the walls. They were as loathe to seek help from the Elves as the Elves were to give it at first - their ancestors having been sworn enemies long ago - but in time each found the other gentler than their old tales would have them believe. When the Djinn-Lord brought a great host against the city, the Orcs swore an oath of alliance with the Elves, and together they routed the invaders, though the Djinn-Lord struck the Elf King dead in the battle.

In the aftermath, under the wise leadership of the King's twin daughters, the Elves opened their gates. Soon many red Orcish yurts complimented the green and gold spires of the Elves, and the great artwork that was the city was complete. As their peoples mixed, they found their skills in smithing to be highly complimentary. The Queens erected public forges and delved mines into the surrounding mountains to feed them.

So Highlake has become a great center of smithcraft, and commerce pours in from every quarter. But even as the city prospers, a darkness lingers on the royal house, and it is said that the Queens spend long hours in their high towers sharpening their minds and magics, their thoughts bent on revenge against the Djinn-Lord. While their thrones go unattended, corruption and ambition have begun to take root around them...

hooks.name: The Queen Is Unwell
hooks.description:
One of the twin queens - Dirue - has seemed unwell lately. She is distracted at public audiences, absent for courtly ceremonies, and spends hours and hours late into the night alone in her tower, from which strange lights have been seen.

Horace Halfheart, proprietor and head editor of the Highlake Herald, feels that exposing the truth behind this change could be to the benefit of the queen's subjects and - incidentally - to the benefit of his publication and himself. As such, he seeks to hire anyone clever enough to get close to the queen and discover the truth.
hooks.gmNotes:
The queen is of course closely guarded by the elite palace forces, and her sister will readily come to her defense, saying that their father's death has been hard on her. It will take either some clever social maneuvering or a bold and stealthy foray onto the palace grounds to gain direct access to Dirue.

Should Our Heroes manage this, they will find that Dirue has made contact with a deity of violence and is in the process of committing herself to its service so that she may use its power to avenge her father's killing.

Here there should be a twist. Perhaps the deity is leading her on with promises so that it may ensnare or devour her. Or perhaps she obtains and makes known her newfound power, and Horace Halfheart is forced to reveal that he is a servant of an opposing deity, and it falls to Our Heroes to choose a side or attempt to contain the ensuing battle.

hooks.name: The Djinn-Lord Returns
hooks.description:
After years of peace, word has reached Highlake that the fearful Djinn-Lord has declared himself openly once more, establishing a fortress on a mountaintop within a day's march of Highlake. He is capturing and enslaving folk of the villages throughout the region, and they say that his fortress is shrouded in swirling clouds of sand and protected by a fearful veiled warrior. It's only a matter of time before he marches on Highlake again.

The Queens have put out a call for volunteers to set out on a scouting mission to understand the nature of the Djinn-Lord's fortress and defenses to help determine whether Highlake should mount a preemptive offensive.
hooks.gmNotes:
Should Our Heroes take up the call, on the approach, they should come across some villagers who have managed to evade the Djinn-Lord's raids. One of them will tell of how their daughter - a brave warrior - was the first to go missing, and that the Djinn-Lord's fortress appeared shortly after that.

Climbing the mountain, the peak is indeed enveloped in clouds of swirling sand. From those clouds emerges the rumored veiled warrior, who proves to be very fierce, but who is recalled before the battle can conclude.

Pressing on, Our Heroes should come out above the clouds of sand to find a huge disc of sandstone hovering above the peak of the mountain. As they watch, a set of sandy stairs magically extends in a downward arc toward them.

On the platform is the Djinn-Lord's palace, filled with an incredible hoard of treasure and dozens of servants - kidnapped villagers from the surrounding area.

The Djinn-Lord should be very fierce, and the veiled warrior should make a second appearance here. A straight-ahead fight should be a deadly enterprise, and so Our Heroes may pursue a few different avenues here.

For one, it should become clear that the veiled warrior (who is of course the villager's missing daughter) is under the Djinn-Lord's control, but also bears some object - a lamp, a large gemstone, etc. - that suggests she summoned the Djinn-Lord in the first place. The Djinn-Lord has twisted the words of her wish to bind her in servitude. Discovering that wish and breaking that bond could turn the tide.

For another, the dozens of servants are fearful of the Djinn-Lord, but not under his control, so some attempt to organize them might prove fruitful. Perhaps among them is a troupe of musicians, whose songs might provide some sort of boon to Our Heroes.

If the Djinn-Lord becomes desperate, he may resort to animating the riches around him into humanoid defenders made of gold coins and jewels, or causing sections of his palace to crumble beneath his foes' feet.

Victory should grant Our Heroes a great quantity of treasure, a single wish from the defeated Djinn-Lord, and the great favor of the Queens of Highlake.

Feel free to replace the missing daughter with some other missing NPC from earlier in your campaign if you choose.

hooks.name: Curious Bubbles
hooks.description:
The surface of the lake of Highlake is famously placid, but recently, strange bubbles have appeared near its center and its waters have been observed to be very slowly rotating. The lake's depth has never been measured, but is supposed to be very great.

The New Orcish Council is organizing a reconnaissance mission to the bottom, using a new and untested powerful water-breathing spell.
hooks.gmNotes:
The most straightforward thing here would be that some huge and ancient monster has stirred from its long sleep and will soon rise to attack the city.

Another possibility would be a pending invasion from some subterranean force, which aims to drain the lake and launch their attack from the center of the city.

Whatever you choose, things should start with the reconnaissance mission going poorly, with some NPCs being killed, captured or eaten as appropriate, and thus Our Heroes are driven to the surface to warn the city, followed by the inevitable large-scale battle.

If you desire a twist, consider placing one or more conspirators in Highlake who have worked to delay and diminish the city's response to the developments, and who reveal their treachery when the threat emerges.
